prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: B025 as a stand-alone award to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case rests on the discovery chain, not on the unanimous opening ranks: proglucagon processing and GLP-1 secretion (Holst), the biology of GLP-1 and the therapeutic rationale (Drucker), and identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form (Mojsov). That chain was established as physiology before any drug existed, and has been replicated for decades. Long-acting agonists then showed benefit in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal outcome trials. Nothing in round 1 touched maturity or the science. The open points are attribution points, and I think the citation can carry them. Wording that credits 'identification of its active form' states what is established without adjudicating a priority contest that the supplied material does not let me settle.
statement.case_against: The attribution weakness is unchanged and I do not think round 1 resolved it. Priority for the active peptide is contested, Habener is outside the credited names, and a prize naming Mojsov invites a dispute that I cannot adjudicate from the evidence supplied. Excluding Knudsen means the prize honours the discovery side and leaves out the acylated analogues that reached patients. If a majority concluded the achievement is the therapeutic step, this trio would be mis-weighted. I also cannot add a second prize part without removing a GLP-1 name, which would weaken the strongest configuration for the sake of a lesser one.

responses.point: You moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and said you would move back toward Knudsen only if the committee decides the citation should explicitly reward the therapeutic step.
responses.response: I welcome the move, and your condition is the right test. That is a decision about what this prize rewards, and it should be taken openly, not as a workaround for the Mojsov priority question. I would not take it here. The discovery-side contributions are better delineated than the drug-engineering step, and the citation can say that the work enabled incretin-based therapies without crediting the drug design. If the committee did choose the therapeutic emphasis, Knudsen would replace Mojsov only if the priority evidence for the active peptide were judged too weak to name her. I have seen nothing that shows that. So I keep Mojsov.

responses.point: You list B031 (TNF blockade) as your alternative and name Knudsen as the first name to revisit for a therapeutic arm. You also ask whether a second achievement is worth sharing the prize.
responses.response: The chair asked whether a second part is worth it. My answer is no for this year. Any second part would take one of the three names away from B025, and every B025 name is load-bearing: a physiologist, a biologist of the hormone, and the person who identified the active form. On TNF I move slightly toward you. Feldmann and Maini are a clean pair, and the evidence is mature. I still read it as clinical proof of concept resting on earlier cytokine biology, so I would not trade a B025 place for it. I take your point that a physiology-centred citation can look like under-crediting drug development. That is why the citation has to name the therapies as the consequence.

responses.point: You argue that a prize for physiology and peptide identification keeps the citation anchored in a discovery rather than a company programme, and you ask whether a two-part configuration with B045 would be preferable.
responses.response: I agree with the first half. On a two-part configuration with B045, I do not support it for this year. The three-name limit means Mori and Walter would take two places from the GLP-1 trio. That would drop either Mojsov, whose identification of the active form is the contested piece I am defending, or Holst or Drucker, who are the core of the physiology. A stand-alone B025 is stronger than a split prize. I keep B045 as my first alternative because its attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist, not because I want to combine it now.

responses.point: You ask whether the supplied evidence supports Mojsov's priority over Habener and others, and how the citation should word a contested priority.
responses.response: The evidence supplied does not let me rule on priority between Mojsov and Habener, and I will not claim it does. What I can support is narrower. Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is a documented contribution, and the citation can credit the identification of the active form without saying who was first. My wording does that. If you want the priority evidence examined before the final ballot, I would support it, but I do not see a reading of it that makes the three-name configuration unworkable. Habener's absence is a constraint of the credited list, which the committee cannot change.

uncertainties: Priority for identifying the active GLP-1 peptide among Mojsov, Habener and others, which I cannot verify from the supplied material.
Whether the committee, on reflection, wants the citation to reward the therapeutic step, in which case Knudsen's claim would need to be weighed against Mojsov.
Whether B045 or B051 is the stronger option behind B025: B045 has the cleaner attribution and B051 has the stronger clinical record but its attribution is incomplete without Eshhar.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist. I have co-authored with committee colleague Sten Linnarsson and with Jonas Frisen, neither of whom is a credited name. Shared KI affiliation is not itself a conflict. No change since round 1.
